Main.sentence: Melbourne is the ___E:capital U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Australian_capital_cities)___ and ___E:most populous city U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_in_Australia_by_population)___ of the ___E:Australian state U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/States_and_territories_of_Australia)___ of ___E:Victoria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria_(state))___ , and the second most-populous city in Australia, after ___E:Sydney U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney)___ .

The city's name generally refers to a 2,453 km 2 (947 sq mi) area,  comprising an urban agglomeration of ___E:31 local government areas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_Government_Areas_of_Victoria#Municipalities_of_Melbourne)___ .

The area of Melbourne has been home to ___E:Aboriginal Victorians U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aboriginal_Victorians)___ for over 40,000 years.

Of the five peoples of the ___E:Kulin nation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kulin_nation)___ , the traditional custodians of the land encompassing Melbourne are the ___E:Boonwurrung U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boon_wurrung)___ , ___E:Woiwurrung U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woiwurrung)___ and the ___E:Wurundjeri U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wurundjeri)___ peoples.

In 1803, a short-lived British ___E:penal settlement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penal_settlement)___ was established at Port Phillip, then part of the ___E:Colony of New South Wales U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colony_of_New_South_Wales)___ .

Melbourne was founded in 1835 with the arrival of free settlers from ___E:Van Diemen's Land U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Van_Diemen%27s_Land)___ (modern-day ___E:Tasmania U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tasmania)___ ).

It was incorporated as a ___E:Crown U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Crown)___ settlement in 1837, and named after the then- ___E:Prime Minister of the United Kingdom U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_the_United_Kingdom)___ , ___E:William Lamb, 2nd Viscount Melbourne U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Lamb,_2nd_Viscount_Melbourne)___ .

Declared a city by ___E:Queen Victoria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Victoria)___ in 1847, it became the capital of the newly separated Colony of Victoria in 1851.  During the 1850s ___E:Victorian gold rush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victorian_gold_rush)___ , the city entered a lengthy boom period that, by the late 1880s, had transformed it into Australia's, and one of the world's, largest and wealthiest metropolises.

After the ___E:federation of Australia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federation_of_Australia)___ in 1901, Melbourne served as the interim seat of ___E:government U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_Australia)___ of the new nation until ___E:Canberra U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canberra)___ became the permanent capital in 1927.

Today, Melbourne is culturally diverse and, among world cities, has the seventh-largest ___E:foreign born population U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign_born#Cities_with_largest_foreign_born_populations)___ .

Additional landmarks include the ___E:Melbourne Cricket Ground U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melbourne_Cricket_Ground)___ and the ___E:National Gallery of Victoria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Gallery_of_Victoria)___ .

Melbourne ranked as the ___E:world's most livable city U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_quality_of_life_indices)___ on ___E:the Economist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Economist)___ 's measure for much of the 2010s.

___E:Melbourne Airport U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melbourne_Airport)___ is the second-busiest airport in Australia and the ___E:Port of Melbourne U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_Melbourne)___ is the nation's busiest seaport.

Its main ___E:metropolitan rail U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Railways_in_Melbourne)___ terminus is ___E:Flinders Street station U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flinders_Street_railway_station)___ and its main ___E:regional rail U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rail_transport_in_Victoria)___ and road coach terminus is ___E:Southern Cross station U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Cross_railway_station)___ .

It also has Australia's most ___E:extensive freeway network U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transport_in_Melbourne)___ and the ___E:largest urban tram network in the world U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trams_in_Melbourne)___ .

Areas of Melbourne are known in the ___E:Boonwurrung U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boonwurrung_language)___ / ___E:Woiwurrung U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woiwurrung_language)___ languages as Naarm or Naarm .

___E:Aboriginal Australians U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aboriginal_Victorians)___ have lived in the Melbourne area for at least 40,000 years.

When ___E:British colonists U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colony_of_Victoria)___ arrived in the 19th century, up to 20,000 ___E:Kulin people U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kulin_people)___ from three distinct language groups – the ___E:Wurundjeri U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wurundjeri)___ , ___E:Bunurong U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bunurong)___ and ___E:Wathaurong U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wathaurong)___ – resided in the area.   It was an important meeting place for the clans of the ___E:Kulin nation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kulin_nation)___ alliance and a vital source of food and water.

In June 2021, the boundaries between the land of two of the ___E:traditional owner U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Traditional_owner)___ groups, the Wurundjeri and Bunurong, were agreed after being drawn up by the ___E:Victorian Aboriginal Heritage Council U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victorian_Aboriginal_Heritage_Council)___ .

The borderline runs across the city from west to east, with the ___E:CBD U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melbourne_city_centre)___ , ___E:Richmond U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richmond,_Victoria)___ and ___E:Hawthorn U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawthorn,_Victoria)___ included in Wurundjeri land, and ___E:Albert Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albert_Park,_Victoria)___ , ___E:St Kilda U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_Kilda,_Victoria)___ and ___E:Caulfield U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caulfield,_Victoria)___ on Bunurong land.  However, this change in boundaries is still disputed by people on both sides of the dispute including N'arweet ___E:Carolyn Briggs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carolyn_Briggs)___ .
The name Narrm is commonly used by the broader Aboriginal community to refer to the city, stemming from the traditional name recorded for the area on which the Melbourne city centre is built.
The word is closely related to Narm-narm , being the Boonwurrung word for ___E:Port Phillip Bay U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_Phillip_Bay)___ .
Narrm means scrub in Eastern Kulin languages which reflects the Creation Story of how the Bay was filled by the creation of the Birrarung (Yarra River).
Before this, the dry Melbourne region extended out into the Bay and the Bay was filled with teatree scrub where boorrimul (emu) and marram (kangaroo) were hunted.

The first ___E:British U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Empire)___ settlement in ___E:Victoria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria_(Australia))___ , then part of the ___E:penal colony U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penal_colony)___ of ___E:New South Wales U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_South_Wales)___ , was established by Colonel ___E:David Collins U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Collins_(lieutenant_governor))___ in October 1803, at ___E:Sullivan Bay U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sullivan_Bay,_Victoria)___ , near present-day ___E:Sorrento U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sorrento,_Victoria)___ .

The following year, due to a perceived lack of resources, these settlers relocated to ___E:Van Diemen's Land U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Van_Diemen%27s_Land)___ (present-day ___E:Tasmania U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tasmania)___ ) and founded the city of ___E:Hobart U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hobart)___ .
It would be 30 years before another settlement was attempted.

In May and June 1835, ___E:John Batman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Batman)___ , a leading member of the ___E:Port Phillip Association U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_Phillip_Association)___ in Van Diemen's Land, explored the Melbourne area, and later claimed to have ___E:negotiated a purchase U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batman%27s_Treaty)___ of 2,400 km 2 (600,000 acres) with eight Wurundjeri elders.

However, the nature of the treaty has been heavily disputed, as none of the parties spoke the same language, and the elders likely perceived it as part of the gift exchanges which had taken place over the previous few days amounting to a ___E:tanderrum U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanderrum)___ ceremony which allows temporary access to and use of the land.   Batman selected a site on the northern bank of the ___E:Yarra River U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yarra_River)___ , declaring that "this will be the place for a village" before returning to Van Diemen's Land.  In August 1835, another group of Vandemonian settlers arrived in the area and established a settlement at the site of the current ___E:Melbourne Immigration Museum U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immigration_Museum,_Melbourne)___ .
Batman and his group arrived the following month and the two groups ultimately agreed to share the settlement, initially known by the native name of Dootigala.

Batman's Treaty with the Aboriginal elders was annulled by ___E:Richard Bourke U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Bourke)___ , the ___E:Governor of New South Wales U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_New_South_Wales)___ (who at the time governed all of eastern mainland Australia), with compensation paid to members of the association.

In 1836, Bourke declared the city the administrative capital of the ___E:Port Phillip District U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_Phillip_District)___ of ___E:New South Wales U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_South_Wales)___ , and commissioned the first plan for its urban layout, the ___E:Hoddle Grid U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hoddle_Grid)___ , in 1837.  Known briefly as Batmania,  the settlement was named Melbourne on 10 April 1837 by Bourke  after the ___E:British Prime Minister U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_the_United_Kingdom)___ , ___E:William Lamb, 2nd Viscount Melbourne U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Lamb,_2nd_Viscount_Melbourne)___ , whose ___E:seat U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family_seat)___ was ___E:Melbourne Hall U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melbourne_Hall)___ in the ___E:market town U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Market_town)___ of ___E:Melbourne, Derbyshire U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melbourne,_Derbyshire)___ .
That year, the settlement's ___E:general post office U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Post_Office,_Melbourne)___ officially opened with that name.
Between 1836 and 1842, Victorian Aboriginal groups were largely dispossessed of their land by British colonists.

In 1840, the Superintendent of the ___E:Port Phillip District U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_Phillip_District)___ , ___E:Charles La Trobe U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_La_Trobe)___ issued a directive to banish Aboriginals from the immediate vicinity of Melbourne.
This was enforced later that same year by the mass-arrest and imprisonment of hundreds of Indigenous people during the ___E:Lettsom raid U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lettsom_raid)___ .
However, Aboriginal people still managed to continue living near the settlement and by January 1844 there were said to be 675 residing in squalid camps around Melbourne.

The British Colonial Office had appointed five ___E:Aboriginal Protectors U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protector_of_Aborigines)___ for the Aboriginal people of Victoria, in 1839, but their work was nullified by a land policy that favoured ___E:squatters U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squatting_(pastoral))___ who took possession of Aboriginal lands.

By 1845, fewer than 240 wealthy Europeans held all the pastoral licences then issued in Victoria and became a powerful political and economic force in Victoria for generations to come.  ___E:Letters patent U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Letters_patent)___ of ___E:Queen Victoria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria_of_the_United_Kingdom)___ , issued on 25 June 1847, declared Melbourne a city.  On 1 July 1851, the Port Phillip District separated from ___E:New South Wales U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_South_Wales)___ to become the Colony of Victoria, with Melbourne as its capital.
The discovery of gold in Victoria in mid-1851 sparked ___E:a gold rush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victorian_gold_rush)___ , and Melbourne, the colony's major port, experienced rapid growth.
Within months, the city's population had nearly doubled from 25,000 to 40,000 inhabitants.
Exponential growth ensued, and by 1865 Melbourne had overtaken ___E:Sydney U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney)___ as Australia's most populous city.

An influx of intercolonial and international migrants, particularly from Europe and China, saw the establishment of slums, including ___E:Chinatown U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinatown,_Melbourne)___ and a temporary "tent city" on the southern banks of the Yarra.

In the aftermath of the 1854 ___E:Eureka Rebellion U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eureka_Rebellion)___ , mass public support for the plight of the miners resulted in major political changes to the colony, including improvements in working conditions across mining, agriculture, manufacturing and other local industries.
At least twenty nationalities took part in the rebellion, giving some indication of immigration flows at the time.
With the wealth brought in from the gold rush and the subsequent need for public buildings, a program of grand civic construction soon began.

The 1850s and 1860s saw the commencement of ___E:Parliament House U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parliament_House,_Melbourne)___ , the ___E:Treasury Building U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Treasury_Building,_Melbourne)___ , the ___E:Old Melbourne Gaol U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Melbourne_Gaol)___ , ___E:Victoria Barracks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria_Barracks,_Melbourne)___ , the ___E:State Library U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_Library_of_Victoria)___ , ___E:University of Melbourne U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Melbourne)___ , ___E:General Post Office U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melbourne_GPO)___ , ___E:Customs House U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immigration_Museum,_Melbourne)___ , the ___E:Melbourne Town Hall U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melbourne_Town_Hall)___ , ___E:St Patrick's U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_Patrick%27s_Cathedral,_Melbourne)___ cathedral, though many remained incomplete for decades. [citation needed]
The layout of the inner suburbs on a largely one-mile grid pattern, cut through by wide radial boulevards and parklands surrounding the central city, was largely established in the 1850s and 1860s.
These areas rapidly filled with the ubiquitous terrace houses, as well as with detached houses and grand mansions, while some of the major roads developed as shopping streets.

Melbourne quickly became a major finance centre, home to several banks, the ___E:Royal Mint U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melbourne_Mint)___ , and (in 1861) Australia's first ___E:stock exchange U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Securities_Exchange)___ .

In 1855, the ___E:Melbourne Cricket Club U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melbourne_Cricket_Club)___ secured possession of its now famous ground, the ___E:MCG U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MCG)___ .

Members of the ___E:Melbourne Football Club U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melbourne_Football_Club)___ codified ___E:Australian football U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_football)___ in 1859,  and in 1861, the first ___E:Melbourne Cup U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melbourne_Cup)___ race was held. Melbourne acquired its first public monument, the ___E:Burke and Wills U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burke_and_Wills_expedition)___ statue, in 1864.

With the gold rush largely over by 1860, Melbourne continued to grow on the back of continuing gold-mining, as the major port for exporting the agricultural products of Victoria (especially wool) and with a developing manufacturing sector protected by high tariffs.
An extensive radial railway network spread into the countryside from the late 1850s.

Construction started on further major public buildings in the 1860s and 1870s, such as the ___E:Supreme Court U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_Victoria)___ , ___E:Government House U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_House,_Melbourne)___ , and the ___E:Queen Victoria Market U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Victoria_Market)___ .
The central city filled up with shops and offices, workshops, and warehouses.
Large banks and hotels faced the main streets, with fine townhouses in the east end of Collins Street, contrasting with tiny cottages down laneways within the blocks.

The Aboriginal population continued to decline, with an estimated 80% total decrease by 1863, [citation needed] due primarily to introduced diseases (particularly ___E:smallpox U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smallpox)___  ), frontier violence and dispossession of their lands.
The 1880s saw extraordinary growth: consumer confidence, easy access to credit, and steep increases in land prices led to an enormous amount of construction.

During this "land boom", Melbourne reputedly became the richest city in the world,  and the second-largest (after London) in the ___E:British Empire U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Empire)___ .
The decade began with the Melbourne International Exhibition in 1880, held in the large purpose-built ___E:Exhibition Building U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Exhibition_Building)___ .

A telephone exchange was established that year, and the foundations of ___E:St Paul's U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_Paul%27s_Cathedral,_Melbourne)___ were laid. In 1881, electric light was installed in the ___E:Eastern Market U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Market,_Melbourne)___ , and a generating station capable of supplying 2,000 incandescent lamps was in operation by 1882.  The ___E:Melbourne cable tramway system U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melbourne_cable_tramway_system)___ opened in 1885 and became one of the world's most extensive systems by 1890.

In 1885, visiting English journalist ___E:George Augustus Henry Sala U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Augustus_Henry_Sala)___ coined the phrase "Marvellous Melbourne", which stuck long into the twentieth century and has come to refer to the opulence and energy of the 1880s,  during which time large commercial buildings, grand hotels, banks, ___E:coffee palaces U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coffee_palace)___ , ___E:terrace housing U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terrace_house)___ and palatial mansions proliferated in the city.  The establishment of the Melbourne Hydraulic Power Company in 1886 led to the availability of high-pressure piped water, allowing for the installation of hydraulically powered ___E:elevators U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elevator)___ , which led to the construction of the first high-rise buildings in the city.   The period also saw the huge expansion of a significant radial rail-based transport network throughout the city and suburbs.
Melbourne's land-boom peaked in 1888,  the year it hosted the Centennial Exhibition.
The brash ___E:boosterism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boosterism)___ that had typified Melbourne during that time ended in the early 1890s.
The bubble supporting the local finance and property industries burst, resulting in a severe economic depression.
Sixteen small ___E:land banks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Land_banking)___ and building societies collapsed, and 133 limited companies went into liquidation.

The Melbourne financial crisis was a contributing factor to the ___E:Australian economic depression of the 1890s U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_history_of_Australia)___ and the ___E:Australian banking crisis of 1893 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_banking_crisis_of_1893)___ .
The effects of the depression on the city were profound, with virtually no significant construction until the late 1890s.

At the time of Australia's ___E:federation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federation_of_Australia)___ on 1 January 1901 Melbourne became the seat of government of the federated ___E:Commonwealth of Australia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_of_Australia)___ .

The first federal parliament convened on 9 May 1901 in the ___E:Royal Exhibition Building U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Exhibition_Building)___ , subsequently moving to the Victorian Parliament House, where it sat until it moved to ___E:Canberra U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canberra)___ in 1927. The ___E:Governor-General of Australia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor-General_of_Australia)___ resided at ___E:Government House U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_House,_Melbourne)___ in Melbourne until 1930, and many major national institutions remained in Melbourne well into the twentieth century.

During ___E:World War II U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II)___ the city hosted American military forces who were fighting the ___E:Empire of Japan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empire_of_Japan)___ , and the government requisitioned the ___E:Melbourne Cricket Ground U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melbourne_Cricket_Ground)___ for military use.

In the immediate years after ___E:World War II U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II)___ , Melbourne expanded rapidly, its growth boosted by ___E:post-war immigration to Australia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-war_immigration_to_Australia)___ , primarily from Southern ___E:Europe U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Europe)___ and the ___E:Mediterranean U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mediterranean_region)___ .

While the "Paris End" of Collins Street began Melbourne's boutique shopping and open air ___E:cafe U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coffeehouse)___ cultures,  the city centre was seen by many as stale—the dreary domain of office workers—something expressed by ___E:John Brack U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Brack)___ in his famous painting Collins St., 5 pm (1955).
Up until the 21st century, Melbourne was considered Australia's "industrial heartland".

Height limits in the CBD were lifted in 1958, after the construction of ___E:ICI House U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ICI_House)___ , transforming the city's skyline with the introduction of skyscrapers.
Suburban expansion then intensified, served by new indoor malls beginning with ___E:Chadstone Shopping Centre U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chadstone_Shopping_Centre)___ .

The post-war period also saw a major renewal of the CBD and ___E:St Kilda Road U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_Kilda_Road)___ which significantly modernised the city.  New fire regulations and redevelopment saw most of the taller pre-war CBD buildings either demolished or partially retained through a policy of ___E:facadism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facadism#Melbourne)___ .
Many of the larger suburban mansions from the boom era were also either demolished or subdivided.

To counter the trend towards low-density suburban residential growth, the government began a series of controversial public housing projects in the inner city by the ___E:Housing Commission of Victoria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Housing_Commission_of_Victoria)___ , which resulted in the demolition of many neighbourhoods and a proliferation of high-rise towers.
In later years, with the rapid rise of motor vehicle ownership, the investment in freeway and highway developments greatly accelerated the outward suburban sprawl and declining inner-city population.
The ___E:Bolte U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Bolte)___ government sought to rapidly accelerate the modernisation of Melbourne.

Major road projects including the remodelling of ___E:St Kilda Junction U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_Kilda_Junction)___ , the widening of ___E:Hoddle Street U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hoddle_Highway)___ and then the extensive ___E:1969 Melbourne Transportation Plan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1969_Melbourne_Transportation_Plan)___ changed the face of the city into a car-dominated environment.

Australia's financial and mining booms during 1969 and 1970 resulted in establishment of the headquarters of many major companies ( ___E:BHP U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BHP)___ and ___E:Rio Tinto U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rio_Tinto_(corporation))___ , among others) in the city. ___E:Nauru U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nauru)___ 's then booming economy resulted in several ambitious investments in Melbourne, such as ___E:Nauru House U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nauru_House)___ .

Like many Australian cities, Melbourne has a high ___E:dependency on the automobile U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Car_dependency)___ for transport,  particularly in the outer suburban areas where the largest number of cars are bought.
There a total of 3.6 million private vehicles using 22,320 km (13,870 mi) of road in Melbourne, which has one of the highest lengths of road per capita in the world.

The early 20th century saw an increase in popularity of automobiles, resulting in large-scale suburban expansion and a tendency towards the development of ___E:urban sprawl U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_sprawl)___ —like all Australian cities, inhabitants would live in the suburbs and commute to the city for work.  By the mid-1950s, there were just under 200 passenger vehicles per 1000 people, and by 2013, there were 600 passenger vehicles per 1000 people.

The ___E:road network in Victoria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roads_in_Victoria)___ is managed by the ___E:Department of Transport and Planning U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Transport_and_Planning)___ (DTP) who oversee planning and integration.

Maintenance of roads is undertaken by different bodies, depending on the road. Local roads are maintained by local governments, while secondary and main roads are the responsibility of DTP. Major national freeways and roads integral to national trade are overseen by the Federal Government.
Today, Melbourne has an extensive network of freeways and arterial roadways.
These are used by private vehicles, including road freight vehicles, as well as road-based public transport modes like buses and taxis.

Melbourne has an integrated public transport system based around extensive train, tram, bus and taxi systems. ___E:Flinders Street station U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flinders_Street_railway_station)___ was the world's busiest passenger station in 1927 and Melbourne's tram network overtook Sydney's to become the world's largest in the 1940s.
From the 1940s, public transport use in Melbourne declined due to a rapid expansion of the road and freeway network, with the largest declines in tram and bus usage.

This decline quickened in the early 1990s due to large public transport service cuts.  The operations of Melbourne's public transport system was privatised in 1999 through a franchising model, with operational responsibilities for the train, tram and bus networks licensed to private companies.
After 1996 there was a rapid increase in public transport patronage due to growth in employment in central Melbourne, with the mode share for commuters increasing to 14.8% and 8.4% of all trips.

A target of 20% public transport mode share for Melbourne by 2020 was set by the state government in 2006.  Since 2006 public transport patronage has grown by over 20% and a number of projects have commenced aimed at expanding public transport usage.

The ___E:Melbourne metropolitan rail network U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melbourne_rail_network)___ dates back to the 1850s ___E:gold rush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gold_rush)___ era, and today consists of ___E:222 suburban stations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Melbourne_railway_stations)___ on sixteen lines which radiate from the ___E:City Loop U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_Loop)___ , a mostly-underground subway system around the CBD. ___E:Flinders Street station U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flinders_Street_railway_station)___ , one of Australia's busiest ___E:rail hubs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transportation_hub)___ , serves the entire network, and remains a prominent Melbourne landmark and meeting place.

The city has rail connections with regional Victorian cities run by ___E:V/Line U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/V/Line)___ , as well as direct interstate rail services which depart from Melbourne's other major rail terminus, ___E:Southern Cross station U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Cross_railway_station)___ , in Docklands.

The Overland to ___E:Adelaide U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adelaide)___ departs twice a week, while the ___E:XPT U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_South_Wales_XPT)___ to Sydney departs twice daily.
In the 2017–2018 financial year, the Melbourne metropolitan rail network recorded 240.9 million passenger trips, the highest ridership in its history.
Many rail lines, along with dedicated lines and ___E:rail yards U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rail_yards)___ , are also used for freight.
An assortment of new railways are under construction in Melbourne.

A new heavy rail corridor through the inner city, the ___E:Metro Tunnel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metro_Tunnel)___ , is set to open by 2025, and will reduce congestion on the City Loop. The ongoing ___E:Level Crossing Removal Project U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Level_Crossing_Removal_Project)___ is grade separating much of the network, and rebuilding many older stations.

In June 2022, early works commenced on the ___E:Suburban Rail Loop U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suburban_Rail_Loop)___ , a 90-kilometre underground automated ___E:orbital line U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circle_route)___ through Melbourne's middle suburbs around 12–18 km (7.5–11.2 mi) from the ___E:CBD U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melbourne_CBD)___ .  ___E:An airport rail connection U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melbourne_Airport_rail_link)___ has commenced with early works in Keilor East.

___E:Melbourne's tram network U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trams_in_Melbourne)___ dates from the 1880s land boom and, as of 2021, consists of 250 km (155.3 mi) of double track, 475 trams, ___E:25 routes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Melbourne_tram_routes)___ , and 1,763 ___E:tram stops U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tram_stop)___ , making it the largest in the world.

In 2017–2018, 206.3 million passenger trips were made by tram.  Around 75 per cent of Melbourne's tram network shares road space with other vehicles, while the rest of the network is separated or are ___E:light rail U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Light_rail)___ routes.

Melbourne's trams are recognised as iconic cultural assets and a tourist attraction. ___E:Heritage trams U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/W-class_Melbourne_tram)___ operate on the free ___E:City Circle route U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_Circle_tram)___ around the CBD.
